advances: Proves the registered single-midpoint ratio and the sheared unimodular-cell erosion certificate with the exact factor \(1/(2e)\). Thus any separate lower bound \(\mathfrak P(C)\geq \eta 2^{-n}W\) would imply mixed depth at least \((\eta/(2e))2^{-n}W\), but no such lower bound is asserted here.
author: research-agent
external_sources:
András Prékopa, “On logarithmic concave measures and functions,” Acta Scientiarum Mathematicarum (Szeged) 34 (1973), 335-343, Theorem 6 on p. 342, primary-source PDF https://rutcor.rutgers.edu/Prekopa/pdf/SCIENT2.pdf and repository record https://acta.bibl.u-szeged.hu/14411/. Exact theorem used: if \(f(x,y)\) is log-concave on \(\mathbb R^{r+s}\) and \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^s\) is convex, then \(x\mapsto\int_A f(x,y)\,dy\) is log-concave. Applicability: \(f(y,v)=\mathbf1_E(v,y)\) is a measurable log-concave function because \(E\) is compact and convex, \(A=\mathbb R^n\) is convex, and the resulting marginal is exactly \(\rho(y)\).

László Lovász and Santosh Vempala, “The Geometry of Logconcave Functions and Sampling Algorithms,” Random Structures & Algorithms 30(3) (2007), 307-358, Lemma 5.12, DOI https://doi.org/10.1002/rsa.20135, author-hosted primary manuscript https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~vempala/papers/logcon.pdf. Exact theorem used: if \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R_+\) is a log-concave probability density and \(H\) is any halfspace containing its centroid, then \(\int_Hf\geq1/e\). Applicability: \(f=\rho/V\) is a Borel, integrable, log-concave probability density with compact support and centroid \(\bar y\); when \(b\neq0\), \(B_b\) is a closed halfspace containing \(\bar y\). Its boundary has Lebesgue measure zero, so the source's halfspace convention does not affect (23). The case \(b=0\) is handled directly and does not invoke the theorem.
proof:
Compactness of the base projection of \(C\) implies that only finitely many fibers \(C_z\), \(z\in\mathbb Z^n\), are nonempty. Hence all sums below are finite. Empty fibers and nonempty lower-dimensional fibers both have \(w_z=0\).

For the first assertion, first note that
\[
w_z w_{z'}>0,\quad z\equiv z'\pmod 2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
w_{(z+z')/2}>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, a compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R^d\) has positive \(d\)-volume exactly when it has nonempty interior. Thus \(C_z\) and \(C_{z'}\) each contain an open ball. Their Minkowski midpoint contains an open ball, and convexity of \(C\) gives
\[
\frac12C_z+\frac12C_{z'}\subseteq C_{(z+z')/2}.
\]
The same-parity assumption makes \((z+z')/2\) integral, proving (1). In particular, if \(w_m=0\), then every product \(w_z w_{2m-z}\) is zero, so
\[
w_m=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A_m=0.
\tag{2}
\]

For \(r\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\), put
\[
W_r:=\sum_{z\equiv r\pmod 2}w_z.
\]
Every ordered same-parity pair \((z,z')\) has the unique integer midpoint \(m=(z+z')/2\), including the diagonal pairs \(z=z'\). Conversely, every term in \(A_m\) is one such ordered pair. Therefore
\[
\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^n}A_m
=\sum_{r\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n}W_r^2
\geq 2^{-n}\left(\sum_rW_r\right)^2
=2^{-n}W^2,
\tag{3}
\]
where the inequality is Cauchy-Schwarz over the \(2^n\) parity classes, including classes of zero mass.

The finite set \(M_+:=\{m:w_m>0\}\) is nonempty because \(W>0\). By (2), (3), and \(\sum_{m\in M_+}w_m=W\),
\[
\sum_{m\in M_+}w_m\frac{A_m}{w_m}
=\sum_mA_m
\geq 2^{-n}W^2.
\]
Thus the \(w_m/W\)-weighted average of \(A_m/w_m\) over \(M_+\) is at least \(2^{-n}W\). Some \(m\in M_+\) consequently satisfies \(A_m/w_m\geq2^{-n}W\), which is the first assertion and also proves \(w_m>0\). This argument includes every zero-fiber case: zero endpoint volume gives a zero summand, while a positive reflected product forces positive midpoint volume by (1).

We prove the second assertion. Fix \(L,m,U\) as in the statement, abbreviate
\[
D:=D_{L,m},\qquad E:=D^-_{L,m,U},\qquad V:=V_{L,m,U},
\]
and assume first that \(V>0\). The shear \(T_L\) is an invertible linear map with determinant one. It fixes the base coordinate and acts on every integer fiber by a translation in the continuous coordinate. Thus \(K=T_L(C)\) is a convex body, and \(T_L\) preserves mixed-integer volume fiber by fiber.

The two affine maps
\[
(v,y)\longmapsto(m+v,y),\qquad
(v,y)\longmapsto(m-v,y)
\]
are bijections of \(\mathbb R^{n+d}\). Hence \(D\) is compact and convex. It is invariant under
\[
R(v,y):=(-v,y).
\tag{4}
\]
Moreover,
\[
E=\bigcap_{q\in Q_U}\{(v,y):(v+q,y)\in D\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Every set in the intersection is closed and convex, and the \(q=0\) member is \(D\). Therefore \(E\) is a compact convex Borel set. Since \(Q_U=-Q_U\), (4) and (5) imply \(R(E)=E\): if \((v,y)\in E\) and \(q\in Q_U\), then \((v-q,y)\in D\), so symmetry of \(D\) gives \((-v+q,y)\in D\). Because \(V>0\), \(E\) is full-dimensional and hence is a convex body in \(\mathbb R^{n+d}\).

For \(y\in\mathbb R^d\), set
\[
E_y:=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:(v,y)\in E\},\qquad
\rho(y):=\operatorname{vol}_n(E_y).
\tag{6}
\]
The function \(\rho\) is Borel measurable. In fact it is upper semicontinuous. To see this, let \(y_j\to y\). If \(E_y=\varnothing\), compactness of \(E\) shows that \(E_{y_j}\) is eventually empty. If \(E_y\neq\varnothing\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\), compactness similarly gives
\[
E_{y_j}\subseteq E_y+\varepsilon B_2^n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(j\); otherwise a convergent sequence of counterexample points would have a limit in \(E_y\). Hence
\[
\limsup_j\rho(y_j)\leq
\operatorname{vol}_n(E_y+\varepsilon B_2^n).
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) and using continuity from above for the decreasing compact neighborhoods of \(E_y\) proves upper semicontinuity.

The indicator \(\mathbf 1_E(v,y)\) is log-concave, with the usual zero convention, because \(E\) is convex. Prékopa's marginal theorem, applied by integrating in \(v\), therefore proves that \(\rho\) is log-concave. Fubini gives
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^d}\rho(y)\,dy=V.
\tag{7}
\]
The support of \(\rho\) is compact, so its centroid
\[
\bar y:=\frac1V\int_{\mathbb R^d}y\,\rho(y)\,dy
\tag{8}
\]
is well-defined.

The centroid of \(E\) is \((0,\bar y)\). Indeed, (4) makes the \(v\)-component of \(\int_E(v,y)\,d(v,y)\) zero, and (6)-(8) give its \(y\)-component. The centroid of a compact convex body belongs to that body: otherwise strict separation from the body, followed by integration of the separating affine functional over the body, gives an immediate contradiction. Thus
\[
(0,\bar y)\in E.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(0\in Q_U\), (5) and (9) give \((0,\bar y)\in D\), and hence
\[
(m,\bar y)\in K.
\tag{10}
\]
Consequently
\[
p:=T_L^{-1}(m,\bar y)=(m,\bar y+Lm)
\tag{11}
\]
belongs to \(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\). This proves admissibility even for an arbitrary real matrix \(L\).

We next compare every eroded section with symmetric lattice pairs. Define the half-open fundamental cell
\[
P_U:=U[-1/2,1/2)^n.
\tag{12}
\]
Since \(U\mathbb Z^n=\mathbb Z^n\), the cells
\[
\{k+P_U:k\in\mathbb Z^n\}
\tag{13}
\]
form a disjoint tiling of \(\mathbb R^n\), and each has volume \(|\det U|=1\). The half-open convention makes the cell center \(k\) unique even on cell boundaries.

For fixed \(y\), put
\[
D_y:=\{v:(v,y)\in D\},\qquad
N(y):=\#(D_y\cap\mathbb Z^n).
\tag{14}
\]
This count is finite because \(D\) is compact, and it is Borel measurable because it is a finite sum of indicators of compact sections. If \(v\in E_y\) lies in its unique cell \(k+P_U\), then
\[
q:=k-v\in-P_U\subseteq Q_U.
\]
The erosion condition gives \((v+q,y)=(k,y)\in D\). Thus \(E_y\cap(k+P_U)\) can be nonempty only when \(k\in D_y\cap\mathbb Z^n\). Using the exact tiling (13) and the unit cell volume,
\[
\rho(y)
=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}
\operatorname{vol}_n(E_y\cap(k+P_U))
\leq N(y)
\quad\text{for every }y.
\tag{15}
\]

We now prove the halfspace estimate in the sheared coordinates. Let
\[
\widetilde S:=K\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)
\]
and let \(\mu_K\) denote its mixed-integer measure. It suffices first to consider a proper closed halfspace whose boundary contains \((m,\bar y)\), written as
\[
G_0:=
\{(z,y):a\mathbin{\cdot}(z-m)+b\mathbin{\cdot}(y-\bar y)\geq0\},
\qquad (a,b)\neq(0,0).
\tag{16}
\]
Set
\[
B_b:=\{y:b\mathbin{\cdot}(y-\bar y)\geq0\},
\tag{17}
\]
which is all of \(\mathbb R^d\) when \(b=0\), and define
\[
M_{G_0}(y):=
\#\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:(z,y)\in K\cap G_0\}.
\tag{18}
\]
This is again a finite Borel sum, and
\[
\mu_K(K\cap G_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}M_{G_0}(y)\,dy.
\tag{19}
\]

Fix \(y\in B_b\). The finite set \(D_y\cap\mathbb Z^n\) is invariant under \(v\mapsto-v\). If \(v\) belongs to it, then both
\[
(m+v,y),\qquad(m-v,y)
\tag{20}
\]
belong to \(K\), and their defining functional values in (16) are
\[
a\mathbin{\cdot}v+b\mathbin{\cdot}(y-\bar y),
\qquad
-a\mathbin{\cdot}v+b\mathbin{\cdot}(y-\bar y).
\tag{21}
\]
At least one value in (21) is nonnegative. For every nonzero orbit \(\{v,-v\}\), the count \(N(y)\) counts two elements and the two distinct base points in (20) include at least one point counted by \(M_{G_0}(y)\). Distinct nonzero orbits give disjoint pairs of base points. If \(v=0\), then \(N(y)\) counts it once, while \((m,y)\in K\cap G_0\) because \(y\in B_b\). Therefore the central orbit is not lost, and the exact pointwise comparison is
\[
N(y)\leq2M_{G_0}(y)
\qquad(y\in B_b).
\tag{22}
\]
This explicitly accounts for both the double counting of \(v\) and \(-v\) and the exceptional fixed point \(v=0\).

If \(b\neq0\), then \(B_b\) is a closed halfspace containing the centroid \(\bar y\) of the normalized log-concave density \(\rho/V\). The log-concave Grünbaum inequality gives
\[
\int_{B_b}\rho(y)\,dy\geq \frac{V}{e}.
\tag{23}
\]
If \(b=0\), which is precisely the vertical-normal case in (16), then \(B_b=\mathbb R^d\), and (7) gives the stronger identity
\[
\int_{B_b}\rho(y)\,dy=V.
\tag{24}
\]
Combining (15), (19), (22), and either (23) or (24), we obtain in every case
\[
\mu_K(K\cap G_0)
\geq\int_{B_b}M_{G_0}(y)\,dy
\geq\frac12\int_{B_b}N(y)\,dy
\geq\frac12\int_{B_b}\rho(y)\,dy
\geq\frac{V}{2e}.
\tag{25}
\]

Let now \(G\) be any closed halfspace containing \((m,\bar y)\). If \(G\) is proper, write it using a nonzero normal and move its boundary parallel to itself until it passes through \((m,\bar y)\). The resulting closed \(G_0\) has the form (16), contains \((m,\bar y)\), and satisfies \(G_0\subseteq G\). Thus (25) and monotonicity give the same bound for \(G\). This reduction uses only inclusion of closed halfspaces. It neither discards nor splits mass on the moved boundary, so positive mixed mass on a boundary hyperplane causes no problem. If \(G=\mathbb R^{n+d}\), it contains, for example, the proper vertical halfspace
\[
\{(z,y):e_1\mathbin{\cdot}(z-m)\geq0\},
\]
and (25) again gives the bound for \(G\). Hence proper, whole, vertical, and all closed-boundary cases are covered.

Finally, \(T_L\) maps every closed halfspace \(H\) containing the point \(p\) in (11) to a closed halfspace \(G=T_L(H)\) containing \((m,\bar y)\). On the fiber with base \(z\), \(T_L\) is the translation \(x\mapsto x-Lz\), so
\[
\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)=\mu_K(K\cap G).
\tag{26}
\]
Equations (25)-(26) prove
\[
h_S(p)\geq\frac{V_{L,m,U}}{2e}.
\]

When \(V_{L,m,U}=0\), the same numerical lower bound is automatic for any \(p\in S\), and \(S\neq\varnothing\) because \(W>0\). Therefore, for every triple \((L,m,U)\),
\[
\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p)\geq\frac{1}{2e}V_{L,m,U}.
\]
Taking the supremum over all triples proves
\[
\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p)\geq\frac{1}{2e}\mathfrak P(C).
\]
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and write
\[
C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},\qquad
w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z>0,
\]
\[
S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d).
\]
For \(m\in\mathbb Z^n\), define
\[
A_m:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z w_{2m-z}.
\]
Then:

1. There is \(m\in\mathbb Z^n\) such that
\[
A_m\geq 2^{-n}Ww_m.
\]
The selected midpoint can be chosen with \(w_m>0\).

2. Fix arbitrary
\[
L\in\mathbb R^{d\times n},\qquad
m\in\mathbb Z^n,\qquad
U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z).
\]
Let
\[
T_L(z,x):=(z,x-Lz),\qquad K:=T_L(C),
\]
\[
D_{L,m}:=\{(v,y):(m+v,y)\in K,\ (m-v,y)\in K\},
\]
\[
Q_U:=U[-1/2,1/2]^n,
\]
and
\[
D^-_{L,m,U}:=
\{(v,y):(v+q,y)\in D_{L,m}\text{ for every }q\in Q_U\}.
\]
Put
\[
V_{L,m,U}:=\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(D^-_{L,m,U}).
\]
If \(V_{L,m,U}>0\), there is
\[
p\in C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)
\]
such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing \(p\) satisfies
\[
\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\geq \frac{1}{2e}V_{L,m,U}.
\]
This includes vertical halfspaces, the whole space, and closed halfspaces whose boundary carries positive mixed mass. Consequently, with
\[
\mathfrak P(C):=
\sup_{\substack{L\in\mathbb R^{d\times n},\ m\in\mathbb Z^n\\
U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)}}V_{L,m,U},
\]
one has
\[
\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p)\geq\frac{1}{2e}\mathfrak P(C).
\]
